summary: Gifford Pinchot NF summit in Skamania County, WA: a first building before 1934, then an L-4 cab abandoned in the 1960s; gone, and no source describes the site now.

facts.design: First building with living quarters below and a small cupola on the roof (1934 description); an L-4 cab later replaced it
facts.status_note: The L-4 cab was abandoned in the 1960s; the register and FireLookout.com both say it is gone.

visit.trail_note: The road is blocked. Walk the old road and climb the hillside to the summit, a bushwhack of under half a mile (Willhite).

events.note: Willhite: a first lookout building stood on the summit, built before 1934; panoramic photos taken July 6, 1934 show the Yacolt Fire burn area
Pete Paladeni, new to the CCC, spent a week on the lookout while the man on duty went home to Spokane for dental care (2002 interview, as printed by Willhite)
L-4 cab, dated 1937 by the register and FireLookout.com; Willhite says it possibly replaced the first building in 1937
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description uses the Mowich Butte Forest Service lookout house as a reference point
Abandoned in the 1960s; sources give only the decade, so the year is a placeholder
A survey team mentions the lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com date the L-4 cab to 1937. Willhite describes an earlier building before 1934 and says the L-4 cab possibly came in 1937. The story reports both accounts.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 2012 registration date (July 16, 2012) does not appear in the cached register page; its Date Registered field is blank in the fetch, so no registration event is recorded. Access level is left out: no source says whether the site is open, and Willhite's route notes start at a blocked road. Paladeni's account is a 2002 interview as printed by Willhite. The most recent description is Willhite's 2017 photo captions; no source describes remains today. The brief lists kind 'ground'; no source read says how the L-4 cab was mounted, so this is unconfirmed.
